trust_decision.summary: cupsd decides that client-supplied job attribute strings are safe to put in the filter/backend options string (argv[5]) only after control characters are turned into spaces; the scheduler's PWG->PPD mapping copied the fax destination-uris values (tel: number, pre-dial-string) into that string without that step.

landing_point.why: The summary names fax option values and the CVE-2026-34980 sanitizer; grepping for destination-uri/pre-dial-string in scheduler/ leads straight to the destination-uris mapping block in get_options, a few hundred lines above the existing sanitizer loop at scheduler/job.c:4121.

fix_sites.entry_point: IPP Print-Job / Create-Job (+Send-Document) on a fax queue (CUPS_PRINTER_FAX) with destination-uris{destination-uri=tel:...}; reaches get_options via scheduler/job.c:859
same IPP job-creation operations with destination-uris{pre-dial-string}

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The published fix is one block in one function (fix.diff:39-76; commit a9e7e7a3 is the same change on another branch, fix.diff:84-124).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The backend's percent-decoding of faxPrefix (backend/ipp.c:2984) is in a different program (the ipp backend, not cupsd), acts on data cupsd already sanitized, and looks like legitimate tel:-URI unescaping, so a solver can argue it is the backend's own business and outside the scheduler sanitizer.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate fax dialing: the backend percent-decodes phone/faxPrefix, strips 'Custom.'/'None' set by print dialogs, maps ',' to 'p' pauses and keeps dial characters such as '*', '#', '+', '-', '(', ')' (backend/ipp.c:2947-2970, 2984-2989). Pre-dial strings like '9,' or '*70' and tel: URIs with visual separators must still reach the device; a fix that rejects the job or strips all non-digits (or drops percent-decoding) breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: destination-uri (IPP uri tag) with tel: prefix; only the first collection value and first URI read (scheduler/job.c:3899-3900)
pre-dial-string (IPP text tag; text validation permits \n, \r, \t: cups/ipp.c:4204)
control characters 0x00-0x1F and 0x7F replaced by space; values truncated to 255 bytes (fix.diff:48-56, 64-72)

O7_producer.where: scheduler/job.c:3897-3908 (PWG->PPD mapping into pwgppds, appended raw at scheduler/job.c:4156-4164)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Backend decodes percent-escapes in faxPrefix after cupsd sanitized it, then writes the decoded pre-dial string unfiltered into a stderr DEBUG line that cupsd parses for PPD:/ATTR: control lines; an encoded newline survives the scheduler sanitizer (decode-after-check differential).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different program from the scheduler; the input reached it already sanitized; percent-decoding is required for tel: semantics; the phone value right above it is filtered by an allow-list so the block looks already safe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: scheduler/job.c -> backend/ipp.c (scheduler/ to backend/ directory, separate executable); sink parser at scheduler/job.c:5401-5427

O8_uncovered_routes.route: faxPrefix sent directly as a plain job option (text/name attribute) passes the existing sanitizer at scheduler/job.c:4121-4138 unchanged except for control chars, then reaches the same backend decode/print path; the published fix only covers the destination-uris mapping.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It goes through the existing CVE-2026-34980 sanitizer, so it looks covered; the advisory names destination-uris only.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same backend file as above; entry is generic job attributes in scheduler/job.c:3969-4146

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another PWG->PPD mapping that copies a client string (e.g. a page-delivery or output-bin fallback that passes the keyword through when the PPD has no match) into pwgppds unsanitized.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Neighbouring mappings in the same function append to pwgppds, which is emitted raw at scheduler/job.c:4156-4164; a maintainer adding a fallback would copy the destination-uris pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A further FaxOut/IPP-Everywhere option (e.g. a fax cover-sheet or recipient name) that is _httpDecodeURI'd and echoed in a DEBUG line like faxPrefix.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The FaxOut block already decodes and echoes two options with this idiom; adding a third member of destination-uris follows naturally.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _ppdCacheGetMediaType returning a client media-type name when no PPD match exists, which then lands in pwgppds.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already reads a client-controlled NAME value; returning it as a fallback is a plausible convenience change.

O9_family: CRLF / control-character injection into a line-oriented control channel (filter options string and backend stderr PPD:/ATTR: lines parsed by cupsd)

O10_build.toolchain: autoconf ./configure + make (gcc/clang); optional GnuTLS/OpenSSL, Avahi, PAM, libusb
O10_build.project_tests: Unit tests in cups/ (testipp.c, testoptions etc.) and the scheduler system test test/run-stp-tests.sh driven by ipptool .test files; examples/fax-job.test exercises destination-uris. Fax-queue behaviour needs a CUPS_PRINTER_FAX queue in the test cupsd. The fix adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Copy the control-character-to-space loop into the destination-uris block in get_options and stop, never looking at the backend that percent-decodes faxPrefix afterwards.

out_of_scope_notes: scheduler/job.c:4079-4083 and 4093-4097: the IPP_TAG_STRING loops never advance valptr (scans/encodes only the first byte); a separate correctness bug.

scheduler/job.c:4156-4164: pwgppds values are appended without escaping spaces, quotes or backslashes (unlike scheduler/job.c:4134-4136), so a fax value can still split into extra options; this is option injection, not the control-character property.
Scheduler validates only the response with ippValidateAttributes (scheduler/ipp.c:5453), not whole requests; only job-name is validated explicitly (scheduler/ipp.c:1500).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check); CUPS is typically tens of MB with locale files, so neither tiny_repo nor giant_repo is expected.

Did not confirm end to end that cupsd's stderr reader splits backend output on '\n' so a decoded newline in the DEBUG line becomes a separate PPD:/ATTR: line; the inference rests on the handler at scheduler/job.c:5401-5427.
Did not check whether a decoded %00 truncates and whether other filters (non-ipp backends, filter/*) print faxPrefix/phone.
